title: Classic ethyl acetate plant S2 of Piotrowski & Kubica 2021 on chepta@0.6.1 and 0.6.2, stream by stream; closing the plant on 0.6.2
question: Build every unit and stream of the paper's classic plant S2 in the released chepta 0.6.1 through its command line, compare CHEPTA's streams and duties with the paper's Appendix Table A2 and Table 1, and record what CHEPTA refuses; then on chepta 0.6.2 re-run every refusal and try to close the whole plant (all recycles) as one CHEPTA flowsheet.
written_by: CHEPTA-Lab worker sessions (Claude); runs on chepta@0.6.1 (2026-11-12) and chepta@0.6.2 (2026-11-13), each executed by the session that wrote that part

sources.note: Every paper number comes from streams.json (Table A2) and equipment.json (Table 1, Figure 1), transcribed 2026-10-29 and audited (STREAM_EQUIPMENT_AUDIT.md); the PDF (sha256 0057df76..., the same as recorded in streams.json) was re-read for this study and is not redistributed.

engines.note: Released npm package installed with npm in a separate folder (its lock file copied as chepta-0.6.1.npm-lock.json); Lab's package.json pin was not changed by this study. Called through its command line, chepta request <file>.

Released npm package installed with npm in a separate folder (lock file chepta-0.6.2.npm-lock.json); Lab's package.json and data/upstream.json not changed. Called through its command line, chepta request <file>.

variants.description: CHEPTA's component records of the four components (molar masses, property ranges).
The paper's values as printed (15 C acid feed, 70 C condensate and extractor, adiabatic MIX 7) or downstream units with acetic acid as a component: kept to record CHEPTA's refusals.
Every unit alone, its inlets the paper's Table A2 streams; downstream of column 5 (u3-*) without acetic acid.

modifications.description: Acetic acid (0.00-0.01 mass % in the paper) dropped from the inlets of the u3-* runs.

variants.description: Section A (feeds, HTXR 2, MIX 3, KREA 4, SCDS 5, HTXR 6, recycle 7), streams 21 and 27 from Table A2.

modifications.description: Reactor conversion imposed from the paper's streams 5 and 6; feeds at 18 C.

variants.description: Section B (MIX 7, EXTR 8, splitters 9 and 16, columns 11 and 15, water loop, heaters), stream 9 from Table A2 without acetic acid; 1 to 8 extractor stages.

modifications.description: Three components; extractor isothermal at 27 C; MIX 7 outlet saturated liquid.

variants.description: The whole plant: sections A and B coupled across streams 9, 21 and 27 by Lab's runner (successive substitution).

modifications.description: The coupling across the cut is Lab's script, not a CHEPTA flowsheet; acetic acid leaving section A in stream 9 is dropped and reported.

variants.description: CHEPTA 0.6.2's component records of the four components.
Every request that 0.6.1 refused or failed, sent unchanged to chepta 0.6.2.
Units and section A with acetic acid as a component where 0.6.1 refused it (extractor, columns 5, 11 and 15 with two liquids; feeds at 15 C), the paper's inlets.

The whole plant as ONE CHEPTA flowsheet, all four components, all five recycles (7, 15, 21, 24, 27) closed by CHEPTA's own tear streams; splitters by flow (26 = 60,000 kg/h; 25 = 20,000 kg/h or 23 = 95,797 kg/h).

modifications.description: Variants of the column 11 specification, convergence method (Broyden, direct, Wegstein), tear guesses (Table A2 or CHEPTA's own 0.6.1 once-through streams) and column 5 phases; see the run manifest's plants.

variants.description: The plant with streams 27 and 21 fed from Table A2 (outer recycles open), to look for starting guesses.
The closed plant and two unit runs again with strictRanges true (request.options and the flowsheet's solver) and with thermo.missingPairs refuse.

warning_notes.note: CHEPTA warns that its UNIQUAC water + ethyl acetate set comes from data at 273.35-343.55 K and is used above it (the reactor vapour, column 5's lower stages, the bottoms of column 15). Results there rest on extrapolated parameters.

assumptions.statement: The reactor's acetic acid conversion per pass (0.7703) is imposed from the paper's streams 5 and 6; the reactor outlet composition is therefore not a prediction.
assumptions.basis: Paper Eqs. 1-3 lack the catalyst concentration and units. The reactor-evaporator is CHEPTA's conversion reactor with an all-vapour outlet (VF 1), which needs the conversion given; there is no kinetic version of it.

assumptions.statement: Section B is run without acetic acid; the two sections are coupled by Lab's script.
assumptions.basis: CHEPTA 0.6.1 refuses two liquids with acetic acid present (runs *-acid). Not used on 0.6.2: the 0.6.2 plant carries the acid everywhere.

assumptions.statement: On 0.6.2 too the reactor-evaporator is CHEPTA's conversion reactor with an all-vapour outlet (VF 1), its acetic acid conversion per pass (0.7703) imposed from the paper's streams 5 and 6.
assumptions.basis: The paper's rate law lacks the catalyst concentration and units; a kinetic reactor-evaporator is not available.

assumptions.statement: The closed plant is accepted by CHEPTA at a tear tolerance of 3e-4 (5e-4 for variant W): with Broyden the loop plateaus near 2e-4 relative change per iteration and CHEPTA's default 1e-8 is not reached; CHEPTA then loosens its own balance check with the tolerance, so Lab checks the plant balance from the result (feeds 1, 2, 17 against products 16, 25: within 6-8 kg/h of 32,461 kg/h for variant R; 42 kg/h for W).
assumptions.basis: Runs plant62-*-tol3e-4 and -tol5e-4; the maintainer (2026-11-13): the plant must converge even with small deviations from the tables. Superseded for the compared numbers by the settled run plant62-best-init1e-4-tol1e-5 (tolerance 1e-5, started from the saved values): the 3e-4 answer had not settled (ethanol inventory still rising).

assumptions.statement: In the closed plant column 15 is held at 99.99 mass % water in its bottoms (Section 3.5's organics limit) instead of the paper's distillate flow, and column 11 at R/D 3 with a distillate flow (230.4 kmol/h as the paper, or 240 kmol/h tuned towards the 99.9 % product); the product purity is then a result.
assumptions.basis: The maintainer (2026-11-13): the purities at the ends of the columns matter more than the flows. Column 11 on its purity refuses in the loop (OUT_OF_RANGE), and on its product flow the loop runs out of ethanol.

assumptions.statement: Splitter 9 gives stream 26 = 60,000 kg/h; splitter 16 gives stream 25 = 20,000 kg/h (variant W) or stream 23 = 95,797 kg/h (variant R). The paper's plant balance is 27 kg/h short, so W fixes the product flow by the balance and column 11 takes its distillate flow (230.4 kmol/h) as second specification.
assumptions.basis: Table A2 streams 23, 25, 26; STREAM_EQUIPMENT_AUDIT.md (S2 plant -27 kg/h).

assumptions.statement: EXTR 8 is isothermal at 27 C with 2 equilibrium stages (stage count chosen to match the paper's stream 11 ethanol).
assumptions.basis: Table 1's 70 C is refused (the feed boils); the paper's outlets at 27 and 41 C imply an adiabatic extractor, which CHEPTA does not have.

unresolved_inputs.consequence: The reactor cannot be predicted; its conversion is taken from the paper.
unresolved_inputs.next_action: Read Atalay (ref. 36) for the catalyst basis; a kinetic reaction in CHEPTA's all-vapour-outlet reactor would then be needed.

unresolved_inputs.item: Number of stages, contactor type and energy balance of EXTR 8.
unresolved_inputs.consequence: The stage count is calibrated; the extract leaves at 27 C instead of 41 C, so HTXR 19 duty is not comparable.
unresolved_inputs.next_action: None in the paper; an adiabatic extraction block in CHEPTA would remove one assumption.

unresolved_inputs.item: Table 1's duties of HTXR 18 and HTXR 19 look exchanged: HTXR 18 (stream 26, 60,000 kg/h, 27 to 70 C) prints 4332.9 kW and HTXR 19 (stream 20, 139,203 kg/h, 41 to 70 C) 1541.1 kW, while CHEPTA gives 1580 and 5681 kW for them (unit runs); S1 shows the same pattern. HTXR 10 heats stream 11's composition with 26 W per kg/h, HTXR 18 with 72 W per kg/h as printed.
unresolved_inputs.consequence: HTXR 18 and 19 are not compared as printed; the totals of Table 2 are unaffected by a label swap.
unresolved_inputs.next_action: Confirmed by the maintainer's spot check (2026-11-12): the two duties are exchanged in Table 1. Ask the authors.

limitations: Agreement with the paper is agreement between two simulators (Chemcad 7 and CHEPTA 0.6.1, both UNIQUAC with different parameters), not with measurements.
The reactor's conversion is imposed from the paper; reactor outlet composition is not predicted.
On 0.6.1 the whole plant is not one CHEPTA flowsheet: acetic acid forces a cut at stream 9, closed by Lab's script.

On 0.6.2 the whole plant is one CHEPTA flowsheet with acetic acid everywhere. With the paper's own column specifications it does not converge (column 5, NO_CONVERGENCE, ten variants). With the column specifications set by the outlet purities it closes (tear tolerance 3e-4) and, started from that answer, settles (1e-5, change 2.1e-6, balance within 0.1 kg/h). The 3e-4 answer (product 99.67 %) had not settled: excess ethanol was still building up in the recycles. Settled product 99.11 mass % ethyl acetate (paper 99.90 %); column 11's distillate flows that would remove the water do not converge in CHEPTA.

On 0.6.2 no pair was estimated (all six UNIQUAC pairs fitted; qualifications.estimated_pairs empty in every run). Extrapolations CHEPTA listed (result.value.extrapolations) are kept per run in the 0.6.2 run manifest and attached to each compared number in comparison-062.

On 0.6.2 strictRanges true (request.options or the flowsheet's solver.strictRanges) did not refuse the 15 C acid feed that 0.6.1 refused; thermo.missingPairs is refused as an unknown key of a flowsheet (BAD_INPUT). Both are reported to CHEPTA.
The extractor is isothermal at 27 C with a calibrated stage count; the paper's extractor is adiabatic at an unknown stage count.
